nominal_positions.interpretation: Eligibility of the Brāhmaṇas. Saṃhitā somyās teṣām. The negative genitive is a control.
With madhu as the object of drinking. Recited somyaṃ before m.
The drops stokān supply masculine plural agreement.
Sāyaṇa collection and Kāśikā own-sense. One observed ending.
Own-sense in Kāśikā, aggregate of riches in Sāyaṇa.
Second recipient with svāhā; first simple nakṣatrebhyaḥ is the comparison.
Everything desired, with suvatu. Saṃhitā final ṃ before s.
Pada deva-tātim. The plural in the semantic gloss does not alter the singular form.
Maker adjective under Sāyaṇa. Neuter noun also proposed. Indeclinable analysis recorded separately.
Predicate of the two Aśvins with bhavathaḥ. Long ī in the Pada.
Purpose for preservation. Refrain counted once for verses 7–9.
State reading in the prayer with astu. Kāśikā also cites the locus for the maker. No separate gender inferred from the ending.
Edition śaṃtātibhir before atho. Bhattacharya’s śantātibhir is an apparatus spelling.
Second, separately coordinated instrumental of welfare or safety.

source_policy_decisions.decision: Primary somyās with ye brāhmaṇāḥ confirms the unstrengthened eligibility stem. Vasu digital saumya is insufficient to change it.
Mayaṭ supplies a semantic model. The affixes actually selected are plain ya for soma and yat for madhu. Retain the RV annotation discrepancy and the PG745 possession control.
Own-sense and collection construals survive with named owners for the same two forms. Keep AV 7.26.8 in the vṛtti alongside 7.27.8 in the checked edition.
Five positive counts give seventeen. Exact primary chandasyaḥ remains Open. Material vasavya is grammatically licensed but lacks a distinct identified primary here.
Paired offering recipients supply a surface control for gha. The ritual commentators group these deities by their association with time.
Separate sarva and deva. The deva plural paraphrase is compatible with a singular word.
Retain Sāyaṇa’s maker adjective and the alternative noun and indeclinable analyses. An added nominative visarga is Excluded from this Pada.
Two makers, long dual ī. A singular headword in a grammar is not this verse form.
Abstract purpose, Sāyaṇa’s own-sense explanation and Vasu's placement under maker remain attributed. Credit the DATsg once.
Repeated nominative, two distinct instrumental stems and one nasal apparatus variant. Context and grammar leave the PS referent/semantic branch open where ambiguous.
